Placing and adjusting shapes

The shape library, dimensions by number and by handle, colour, rotating, tapering and twisting.

Este capítulo ainda não está traduzido para português de Portugal. Segue-se o texto em inglês.

Every part in layerling starts with a shape. From them you build everything else: shapes complement each other, cut each other out or are joined into a new shape.

Adding a shape

Click «Adicionar forma» in the ribbon. The shape library opens.

The library is one list in sections, from «Formas básicas» to «Auxiliares», each with the number of shapes in it. A click on a section's name folds it away, and the browser keeps what you folded; the first time, all of them are open. On top, «Usadas recentemente» holds the last four shapes you put in. The search field finds a shape by its name and by other words for it, in English and German too: "USB" finds the «Abertura para conector». While you type, only the sections with a match show; an empty field brings your folded sections back as they were. «Formas personalizadas» on top is a single line until you keep a shape there.

The library closes after each shape you pick. Its title bar moves it, so you can put it where it does not cover the spot you are aiming at, over the properties panel for example; a double-click on the title bar puts it back under its button, and where you left it is kept in the browser. The pin in the title bar keeps the library open while you put several shapes one after the other. Its edges and corners pull its size, as wide and as high as your screen allows; the size is kept in the browser too, and a double-click on an edge sets it back. Pulled narrow, the library leaves out the names and shows only the pictures; the name appears when you point at a shape.

Pick a shape. It now hangs on the mouse pointer and lands where you click. Move it over a body and it lies down on the face under the pointer, sloped ones too, like Cruise in Tinkercad; over the empty plate it lands on the workplane. Esc cancels placing. A tool that waits for a click, such as the tape measure, the framing square, a note, «Colocar plano de trabalho», «Assentar sobre uma face» or the edge tools, is switched off when you pick a shape, so the click places the shape. The other way round, switching one of those tools on puts the shape down again. If you would rather have the shape appear in the middle of the plate, you can switch off placing by click in the settings (area «Aspeto», switch «Posicionar sobre faces ao adicionar novas formas»).

On a face the shape snaps to the middle of that face when the pointer comes near it, as a corner or an edge snaps; hold Alt to set it down anywhere. Dragged from the library onto a face instead, it always lands in the middle of the face, or with Alt where you let go.

What the library offers:

  • «Formas básicas»: «Bloco», «Bloco arredondado», «Cilindro», «Cápsula», «Elipse», «Polígono» (three to twenty-four sides), «Cunha», «Esfera», «Cone», «Cone curvo» (its side bends inward into a trumpet like a pseudosphere or outward into a dome; «Diâmetro do topo» and «Curvatura» set it, and it can be hollowed out and filleted like any exact body), «Pirâmide» (with three to twenty-four sides, so three-sided too), «Telhado arredondado», «Hemisfério», «Paraboloide» (a dome that narrows to a rounded tip, its height falling with the square of the distance from the axis) and «Toroide».
  • «Recipientes, tubos e transições»: the «Transição entre perfis» from one outline to another, say from square to round, the «Tubo», the «Tubo curvo», made of up to twelve straight pieces with bends in between, and the «Vaso».
  • «Furos e recortes»: the «Escareado cilíndrico» and «Escareado cónico» for screw heads, the «Furo em forma de gota» for horizontal holes and the «Abertura para conector» for USB, HDMI, DisplayPort and RJ45 sockets.
  • «Ligações»: «Rosca» (threaded rod, screw, nut and tapped hole), the «Anilha de acabamento» under a countersunk screw, the print-in-place «Dobradiça» and the «Cauda de andorinha». More in Threads and mechanics.
  • «Peças para caixas»: the «Pilar de fixação» for heat-set inserts and self-tapping screws, the «Encaixe por pressão» with its catch and the «Nervura» or gusset. More in Threads and mechanics.
  • «Mecânica e peças móveis»: «Mola», «Engrenagem», the «Acoplamento Hirth» and the «Polia GT2».
  • «Sistemas e modelos»: «Gridfinity» bins and baseplates, and the «Placa SBC», a single-board computer true to size to build a case around.
  • «Texto e sinalética»: «Texto», also along a circular arc, the «Placa de identificação», the «Placa com ícone» and the «Código QR». More in Text.
  • «Contornos decorativos»: «Estrela», «Coração», «Lua crescente» and the «Recartilhado» for grips.
  • «Auxiliares»: the «Régua», which is only a measuring tool and never shows up in an export.

You get a triangle in two ways: the «Polígono» with three sides is an isosceles triangle, the "Roof" of Tinkercad, and the «Cunha» is a right triangle. Both are true triangular prisms. For a triangular hole, copy the shape, make the copy smaller, mark it as a hole and line it up with «Centrar no plano de trabalho» or «Alinhar». Both work with the shape's bounding box, the smallest box that encloses it, so a halved square still counts as a whole square. The command search (Ctrl+K) also finds both shapes under "triangle" or "roof".

The «Cápsula» can be narrower at one end than at the other, say for a guard over a belt between two pulleys. Under «Propriedades» set «Extremidade menor (diâmetro)»; the large end is as wide as the capsule, and the sides run straight from one arc to the other. «Distância entre centros» is the distance between the two arcs' centres, that is how far apart the pulleys are. Change the small end and the centre distance stays, the capsule getting longer or shorter. The tapered capsule stays an exact body too, for fillets and STEP.

The shape's settings

As soon as a shape is selected, its settings appear on the right. At the top is the name; the pencil beside it («Mudar o nome») lets you type a new one. Enter keeps it, Esc cancels, and an empty name brings back the shape's default name. Further right, the padlock locks the shape against accidental moving and the eye hides it. The arrow on the far left folds the settings down to their title bar. The cards below fold open and shut with a click on their title («Propriedades», «Posição», «Rotação», «Afunilamento», «Torção e inclinação» and the cards of the special shapes); layerling remembers which ones you left open, for the next shape and the next visit.

The settings sit docked at the right edge. If they cover something you want to see, drag them by their title bar and they float wherever you drop them; they stay there for the next shape too. Drop them back at the top right, or double-click the title bar, and they dock again. While they float or are folded down, the snap step moves from the bottom of the settings to the bottom right of the workplane.

  • «Sólido» or «Forma de corte»: A solid stays, a hole takes material away. A click on «Sólido» opens the colours; colours of your own that you mix there wait under «Usadas recentemente» afterwards, the last eight. More in Solids and holes. The pin in the row «Guardadas» keeps the colour you have chosen for good: it stands in a row of its own, newer colours never push it out, and the same pin lets go of it again; up to 21 colours are kept in this browser.
  • «Transparente»: Lets you see through the body, for example to spot a shape behind it.
  • «Multicor»: For a group or a bundle; Shift+M switches it. Switched on, every part of the group shows in its own colour, also in a group that was cut with holes into one body (the walls a hole leaves take the colour of the body they were cut into). Picking a colour for the group switches it off and colours the whole group; the parts keep their own colours underneath, so switching it on again brings them back. A bundle has it switched on to begin with, and when it is switched off the bundle shows and exports in one colour. A group of solids only that you make starts with it switched off and shows as one body; groups made before keep showing their parts' colours. In a 3MF export every part keeps its colour, so the slicer can map the parts onto filaments; OBJ carries the colours on its points, so the border between two colours is a little rougher there.
  • «Propriedades»: The dimensions and everything that belongs to this shape. For a cylinder the diameter, the height and the number of sides. For a round tube or ring the «Diâmetro exterior», the «Diâmetro interior» (for a bushing on a shaft of a known size) and the wall thickness: any two give the third, in whatever order you type them. The outer diameter keeps the bore and changes the wall, the inner diameter keeps the outer one and changes the wall, and a bore wider than the tube makes the outer diameter grow by the wall. The tube's length is its height. A tube that is not round, after you pulled one of its sides, has the sides Length and Width instead of the one outer diameter; there the wall stays when you change the width. For a gear the teeth, for a spring the turns. A value you have moved away from its default gets a small arrow next to its name: a click takes just that value back, whatever else you did since, unlike Undo. A double click on a slider does the same, here and for the sliders in the workspace settings. Dragged with the mouse, the slider of a length snaps to the snap step, so a height comes out in whole millimetres (not with the grid off, and not on short sliders); a typed value and the arrow keys on the slider stay exact. «Guardar como predefinição» at the bottom makes the current values the start values of this kind of shape (the same as «Predefinições das formas» in the settings), and «Repor predefinições» goes back to the app's own. With «O interior do tubo atua como forma de corte ao agrupar» the bore counts as a hole once the tube is grouped: it then also cuts the wall of what the tube is grouped with, so two tubes in a T-junction open into each other. A bent tube with an opening has the same switch.
  • «Transformar numa elipse»: Only on a cylinder. A cylinder is always round: it has one diameter, and every handle changes both sides together. For an oval, click this and it becomes an «Elipse» - the same body, whose length and width you then set one by one. A cylinder with a chamfer, a fillet or a wall, or a turned or grouped one, cannot be changed this way; take the «Elipse» from the start for those.
  • «Afunilamento»: Different sizes at the top and bottom, for example for a slope or a funnel. With «Manter proporções» switched on, Length and Width of the same end change together in the ratio they have, so a square top stays square; top and bottom stay separate.
  • «Torção e inclinação»: Twists the top against the bottom or shifts it sideways. That gives twisted columns and leaning towers.
  • «Inclinar ao longo»: Runs the top down towards one end. «Extremidade mais baixa» picks the end, «Altura da extremidade» or «Inclinação (°)» how low it goes, and «Curvatura (%)» whether the top runs straight (0), bulges up (above 0) or sags (below 0). The other end keeps the body's height. Once it is set, an orange dot sits on the top of the lower end; drag it up and down like the height. That gives a roof whose height runs down along its length, a ramp or a slanted pipe end.
  • «Estreitar ao longo»: Seen from above, runs both long sides in evenly towards one end, so that end stays in the middle. «Extremidade mais estreita» picks the end, «Largura da extremidade» its width (0 makes a point), «Início em (%)» where along the length the narrowing begins (0 % at the wide end, 50 % in the middle), and «Curvatura (%)» whether the sides run straight (0), bulge out like a boat's bow (above 0) or are drawn in (below 0). Its orange dot sits on the side of the narrow end and moves across. Together with «Inclinar ao longo» it makes a bow or a ridge that runs down and in at once.

Taper and twist work on almost every shape. Only the gear, thread, spring, Gridfinity, hinge, pyramid, bent tube, teardrop, port opening, the screw-head cutters and the ruler leave them out: they have fixed measures of their own or, like the pyramid, a top of their own already.

«Guardar como predefinição» keeps what you changed on this shape as the start of every new shape of its kind: the sizes, the settings of the shape and its colour. Colour a cylinder green, press the button, and every cylinder you add from then on is green; the other kinds keep their own colours. «Repor predefinições» takes the kind back to what the app starts it with. The kinds that have defaults of their own are marked in the settings under «Predefinições das formas». A new design that you start from the start page begins with them too; the values are kept in this browser.

A tapered or leaning box, cylinder, ellipse, polygon, tube or ring keeps its exact shape, and so do the capsule, star, heart, crescent, dovetail a rounded box without rounded top and bottom edges, and a straight or round knurl (its chamfered ends narrow with it): chamfers and fillets work on it as on the plain shape, and the STEP export writes it. The same holds for a twisted shape: its section turns exactly as it rises, and the sides wind evenly from bottom to top.

«Inclinar ao longo» is offered on the box, rounded box, cylinder, ellipse, polygon, tube, ring, wedge and round roof. The wedge and the round roof lie along their depth, so they slope to the front or the back only. The sloped body keeps its exact shape, so chamfers, fillets and the STEP export work on it as on the plain shape; only a rounded box with rounded top and bottom edges, and a slope together with a taper, a twist or a lean, stay on the display mesh.

«Estreitar ao longo» is offered on the same shapes except the tube and the ring, whose wall would get thinner across than along. A narrowed box, and a wedge or round roof narrowing, sloping or both, keep their exact shape in the same way. For now the display mesh only covers the rest: a narrowed cylinder, ellipse, polygon or rounded box, and a box that slopes and narrows at once. Chamfers, fillets and the STEP export then work on that mesh rather than on an exact body.

Typing is more exact than dragging. All number fields take millimetres, but also percentages: type "50 %" into a width of 40 mm and you get 20 mm. They calculate too: "15*3", "120-2*4" or "(40+2)/2" give 45, 112 and 21; x works instead of *. The field remembers the calculation, in the properties panel as well as in the dimension boxes around the selected body: click into it again later and the formula stands there instead of the number, as long as the value still matches it, and you change it in place, "(140+2)/2" becoming "(40+6)/2". Drag the body by a handle or scale it and the formula no longer fits, so the field shows just the number again. In a number field you have clicked, the mouse wheel and the keys ↑ and ↓ change the value by one step, with Shift a larger step and with Alt a finer one. In a size or position field Shift steps by the snap grid instead, and by ten steps when the grid is off. It also works without clicking into a field: hold the mouse button down on the name of a value, say "Width", and drag left or right; the value changes as you drag, with the same keys as the wheel.

Choosing colours

A click on «Sólido» in the properties of a body opens the colour card, headed «Cor da forma». On top it shows the hex value of the colour the body has now. Under it are the ready colours of the palette; a click on one colours the body and closes the card.

«Personalizado» opens the colour picker of your browser, for a colour of your own. What it offers depends on the browser: in Chrome and Edge it has a colour field, a slider for the hue, an eyedropper that takes a colour from anywhere on the screen, and the value as HEX, RGB or HSL, which you switch with the arrows beside it. The colour counts when you close the picker or click outside it.

A colour of your own that you mix there waits under «Usadas recentemente» afterwards, the last eight. The pin in the row «Guardadas» keeps the colour you have chosen for good: it stands in a row of its own, newer colours never push it out, and the same pin lets go of it again; up to 21 colours are kept in this browser. The pin is for colours of your own, the ones of the palette are always there. With several colours selected, or with a hole, there is no single colour to keep.

The colours of the work area in the settings have a simpler picker of their own, with a colour field, a row of ready colours and a field for the hex value; see The settings.

How round is round? The side count

Round shapes such as cylinder, cone, tube, ellipse or the bores have the switch «Número de lados acompanha o tamanho» and the slider «Lados» in their properties. The «Toroide» has two sliders: «Lados do anel» around the ring and «Passos do tubo» around the tube. They follow the size there too until you hold them, so a large torus shows no facets. The reason: for the view and for STL, 3MF and OBJ, layerling draws a circle as a polygon of many small sides. The more sides, the smoother it is, and the more triangles it takes.

The «Espessura do tubo» sets how thick the tube is seen from above. The height only squashes or stretches the tube, so a flat ring keeps its hole; at half the outer size the hole closes. Dragging the handles scales the tube along. Only a torus whose tube is as thick as the torus is high stays an exact body for chamfers, fillets and STEP.

Where the side count matters

  • In the export for the slicer (STL, 3MF, OBJ). A cylinder with few sides arrives there as a polygon.
  • When bodies and holes are combined. A bore cut by a hole with few sides is angular in the finished part. That includes screw holes.
  • In the view. Many very fine shapes slow the editor down.

Where it does not matter

  • For the STEP export. It writes the round shape, not the polygon.
  • For chamfers and fillets («Chanfrar», «Arredondar») as long as the shape stays round. That is the case when you have not set a side count, when the count is at least the shape's default, or when the polygon strays at most 0,05 mm from the circle. The default is 96 sides for cylinder, ellipse, tube and cone, 64 for the «Telhado arredondado», 24 steps for the «Esfera», 32 for the «Hemisfério» and the «Paraboloide», 96 sides and 24 steps for the «Toroide», and a «Qualidade» of 32 for a round «Tubo curvo».
  • For a thread, a spring or a helical or herringbone gear. The edge tool and the STEP export take its exact body; its «Qualidade» only sets how finely it is drawn.

Where it matters again

  • For chamfers and fillets on a shape with few sides. If you set the side count below the default, the edge tool takes the shape as it is drawn: a cylinder with 6 sides stays a hexagonal bar, and the fillet runs round its six edges. That is how you can build, for instance, a nut pocket with rounded corners. For a round shape, leave «Número de lados acompanha o tamanho» on.

How to use it

  • Leave «Número de lados acompanha o tamanho» on. Then layerling picks the side count from the diameter so that the polygon strays at most 0,005 mm from the true circle, far below what a printer resolves. Small shapes get at least 24 sides, large ones more.
  • Fewer sides you take when you want a polygon on purpose (but there is the «Polígono» for that) or when the editor gets slow with very many round shapes.
  • More sides you hardly ever need. Only on very large round parts, when you see edges in the STL.
  • For parts you only treat with edges or hand on as STEP, the side count does not matter.

Working with the handles

Besides the settings there are handles on the shape itself:

  • The corners and edges make the shape larger or smaller. Drag one past the opposite side and the shape keeps growing there, on the other side of that edge. The arrow on top does the same below the base. Hold Shift while dragging a corner to scale width, depth and height together and keep the proportions; hold Alt to scale from the center instead of the opposite corner. Without a keyboard, or if you do not want to hold a key, switch on «Manter proporções» at the top of the properties: then the corners always keep the proportions, and typing one of width, depth or height scales the other two by the same factor. The setting is remembered.
  • The black arrow above the shape lifts or lowers it; with Alt held from the start, a copy is made where you let go, so you can stack. The handle on the top face changes the height. The handles that change one measure carry the colour of its axis, as the curved arrows do: the middle of a side (width red, depth green) and the top (height blue); the corners change two measures and stay white.
  • The red and the green arrows on top move the shape along X or along Y only. The shape then follows the mouse along that line, even when you look at the plate from low down, where a free drag runs off far. It snaps to other shapes as a drag does, and afterwards you can click the distance moved and type the exact value.
  • The curved arrows rotate it.
  • The numbers beside the shape show the dimensions. A click on one opens a field in which you type the number you want. With Enter the shape grows from the edge opposite the number, as when you drag; with Alt+Enter it grows round its middle, so a shape that was aligned with another stays aligned. With «Manter proporções» ticked in the properties, or with Shift+Enter, the other two dimensions follow by the same factor. That holds for width and length; the height always grows upward from the underside. The fields in the properties on the right keep the middle without a key. Tab keeps the number and opens the next one (width, depth, height); Shift+Tab goes back. In a field of the properties that you have clicked, the mouse wheel changes the value as well: a unit a notch, ten times as much with Shift (in a size or position field the snap grid), a tenth with Ctrl and a hundredth with Alt. A field that you have not clicked leaves the wheel to the panel, which scrolls.
  • A click on a corner (without dragging) opens width and depth together. Type the first, press Tab for the second and Enter to apply both. Esc cancels.

Once a shape is turned by right angles, for instance laid on its side with «Assentar sobre uma face», the fields in the properties are named after the direction each measure runs in now: «Altura» is what goes up, «Largura» runs along X and «Comprimento» along Y. Typing the height of a shape lying down therefore changes the vertical measure, and its underside stays on the plate. A shape tilted at any other angle shows its own measures in the fields, and a note below says so.

Without the mouse, use the keyboard: the arrow keys move the selection by one snap step (0.01 mm when the grid is off), with Shift by five, or by ten if you set «Linha da grelha mais escura a cada» to «10 intervalos da grelha» in the settings under «Aspeto»: as far as the next darker line, as in Tinkercad. They follow the view: → moves to where the screen's right is, ↑ away from you, even after turning the plate. Push a shape out of the picture and the view moves along. Ctrl+↑ and Ctrl+↓ raise and lower it. A run of arrow presses is one step in the history: as long as the next press follows within a second and a half, Undo takes back the whole run, not a press at a time. R rotates by 45°, Shift+R by 22.5°. D drops the selection onto the workplane.

The handles pull a shape as large as your plate, at least 220 mm wide and deep. Typing a number in the properties goes beyond that, and a shape made that large does not shrink back when you grab it again. A ceiling of your own per shape is set in the settings under «Predefinições das formas» with «Limite de tamanho personalizado».

The snap step is at the bottom right of the editor and can be changed at any time.

Copying and duplicating

«Copiar», «Colar» and «Duplicar» are in the ribbon («Área de transferência»). Ctrl+D duplicates a selection. layerling remembers how you last moved or rotated the copy and applies the same again on the next duplicate. That produces a row of holes or steps in a few key presses. For regular arrangements there is also the pattern, described in Selecting and arranging. If you also resized the copy, every further copy grows by the same factor again, as in Tinkercad. A shape you gave a name of your own gets a copy that is called after it, "Holder (copy)", then "Holder (copy 2)" and so on, so the object list stays readable; a shape that only has the name layerling handed out ("Box") keeps it.

Tip: If a shape refuses to take the size you want, it is often the limits for new shapes. Under «Predefinições das formas» in the settings you decide how each shape starts and how large it may get.

Custom shapes

A holder, a grip or a base plate you need again and again goes into the «Formas personalizadas». They sit at the top of the shape library, above the «Formas básicas», and fold away with their arrow.

  1. Select one or more bodies, holes, groups or an imported model included.
  2. Open the shape library and click «Guardar seleção». Enter a name and confirm with «Guardar».
  3. In any design, a click on the tile inserts the shape, like any other shape. You can also drag the tile onto the workplane; it then lands where you let go. The shape then hangs on the pointer, like any other: it follows it, also over the faces of other bodies, and a click sets it down; Esc puts it away.

Several bodies come back together, placed as they stood to each other, and stay selectable one by one. Notes pinned to the saved bodies go along and come back closed, pinned to the inserted ones; free notes and reference points stay in the design. The pencil on a tile renames it, the bin removes it after asking. Shapes already inserted into designs stay as they are.

The «Formas personalizadas» live in this browser, apart from the designs, and are there again the next time you start. «Criar cópia de segurança de tudo» on the start page backs them up with the designs, and opening the backup brings both back. To take only the shapes to another browser, «Criar cópia de segurança das formas personalizadas» (the arrow pointing down) saves them as a ZIP file and «Carregar formas» (the arrow pointing up) brings them back there. «Carregar formas» also takes single .lyl designs; each one becomes a shape. Shapes already there are not added twice.

Folders

Many custom shapes sort better into folders. «Nova pasta» (the folder with the plus, next to «Guardar seleção») asks for a name and makes a folder at the top; the folder with the plus on a folder, «Nova subpasta», makes one inside it. Folders go three levels deep: a folder on the third level holds shapes but no further folders. Folders sit above the shapes that are in none, in the order of their names, and open and close with their arrow; the number on a folder counts the shapes in it and in the folders inside it. When saving, choose the folder in the list next to the name; «Sem pasta» keeps the shape at the top.

The folder with the arrow on a tile moves that shape into another folder, or back out with «Sem pasta». The pencil on a folder renames it, the bin deletes it after asking, together with the folders and shapes in it. A folder itself cannot be moved: make the new one where it belongs and move the shapes over. A backup keeps the folders, and loading it puts the shapes back in the same place.

Custom shapes on the server

With the shared server store switched on, the section shows two groups: «No servidor» and «Neste navegador». When saving you choose where the shape goes; the server is chosen to start with. There it lives in the folder Custom shapes, as a .lyl file of its own with a picture, ready on every device that reaches the server; its folders are folders inside Custom shapes. Each side has folders of its own, and a shape moves between the folders of its side. The cloud on a browser tile puts that shape on the server; it is then no longer kept twice.

The Custom shapes folder shows on the start page as well. Open a shape there like a design, change it, and it is saved automatically like any design on the server; the next insert takes the new version. As the server store has no login, everyone who reaches the server sees the same shapes.

Wrapping around a cylinder

Should a pattern, a logo or lettering go onto a cup, a can or a tube? First lay it flat on the plate, as an imported SVG or as text for example, the way it should look from above. Then wrap it around a cylinder in the shape's settings under «Envolver em torno de um cilindro»:

  1. Open «Envolver em torno de um cilindro» and enter the «Diâmetro» of the cylinder wall, such as the outside diameter of your cup. Tenths of a millimetre work too, such as 63.5.
  2. Click «Envolver». What ran from left to right now runs around the cylinder, the back edge becomes the top, and the thickness stands out of the wall.
  3. Select the wrapped shape and the cylinder and centre both, left to right and front to back. The middle of the wrapped shape is the cylinder's axis, so it then sits right on its wall.

Every body can be wrapped, a shape from the library too: a round roof, say, that should sit on the wall of a round tower. Lay it on the plate the way it should look on the wall, its round top at the back.

For an engraving, switch on «Para dentro (gravação)»: the thickness then goes into the wall. Make the shape a hole, centre it and group it with the cylinder.

A shape that is wrapped already is a mesh of the wrapped thing and cannot be wrapped again: undo the wrapping, or wrap the flat original once more with another diameter.

The result is a mesh like an imported model. Undo lays the shape flat again; for another diameter, undo first and wrap again. It cannot go further than once around the cylinder; then layerling names the smallest diameter that fits.

A surface texture

Grooves, knurling, honeycomb or bumps on a body, for a better grip or for looks: open «Textura de superfície» in the shape's settings. The button «Textura de superfície» in the «Modificar» group at the top does the same: it opens and closes the card for the selected body and stays lit while the card is open.

  1. Choose the «Padrão», its «Espaçamento» and its «Profundidade». «Direção» says whether it goes into the body or stands out of it. For «Saliências», «Forma da saliência» chooses between «Semiesfera», «Cone (pontiagudo)», «Suavemente arredondada» and «Topo plano». Under «Disposição» they sit «Desencontrada», every other row half a spacing along, or in «Filas alinhadas».
  2. Under «Projeção», take «Em redor de um eixo» for round bodies such as a cup, a knob or a handle. The pattern runs round the «Eixo», and the spacing is rounded a little so that a whole number of grooves or cells goes round: the pattern closes without a seam. «Em toda a volta» suits bodies that are not round, «Plana, ao longo do eixo» a lid or a plate seen from above. Leave it at «Automático» and Layerling chooses for you: «Em redor de um eixo» on round bodies and on angular ones standing upright such as a box - the pattern then follows the outline and runs round the edges without a seam, a pattern standing out bending round them -, «Em toda a volta» on other angular ones.
  3. Click «Aplicar textura». A large body takes a few seconds; you can keep working meanwhile.

To give the pattern to only some faces, say only the top of a box, click «Selecionar faces» and then the faces in the view: the top, the bottom or a side. A face reaches up to the body's sharp edges; on a cylinder the mantle is one face, and the top and the bottom are one each. Picked faces light up, a second click takes one out again, and «Voltar a usar todas as faces» gives the pattern the whole body again. Only the picked faces get the pattern; all others stay as they were and keep few triangles. On a top or a bottom the pattern lies flat; on a round top, grooves, rope and knitting run in rings round the middle, like a tree's year rings. «Direção no topo e na base (°)» turns the pattern on the top and bottom: at 0° the rows run along the front edge, at 90° along the side edge. «Topo e base» switches grooves, rope and knitting there between rows and rings; on an angular body the rings follow its outline. «Aresta no topo e na base» says what happens at the edge between the side and a patterned top or bottom: «Viva» lets both end at the edge. With «Padrão lateral prolongado» the side's pattern bends round the edge and takes the whole top: rows of rope, knitting and level grooves run on as rings, upright and slanted grooves as rays almost to the middle. «Dobra curta» does the same as a rim only; inside lies the top's own pattern, as «Topo e base» sets it. «Rebordo» lays a border round the edge for every pattern – a cord, a cast-off chain or a round bead. A tight round (a fillet) ends a face as well: on a cup with rounded rims the outside, the rounds, the rim, the inside and the bottom are faces of their own, so a click on the outside takes only the outside. A wide round, about a quarter of the body or more, belongs to the face, as a sphere is one face. With picked faces, «Paredes exteriores» and «Paredes interiores» do not count.

Several patterns on one body – bricks round the sides, knurling on the top – are layers: «Camada» beside the first adds one, and picking is switched on for it at once; click the faces it should get. Every further layer goes only on its own faces, the first on all the others. The tabs show one layer at a time with its settings, «Remover esta camada» takes one away. All layers are made together on the body under the texture, so changing one or taking the texture off works as for a single pattern. A text needs no faces as a layer: it goes where it is put.

Under «Mais» you choose where the pattern goes: outer and inner walls, how far the bottom and the top stay smooth (a smooth bottom keeps the body flat on the bed), a band of the height, and whether sharp edges stay smooth. Next to everything that stays smooth, the pattern fades in gently; «Desvanecer ao longo de» sets over how many millimetres. The smaller it is, the closer the pattern comes to an edge; a pattern standing out runs out right up to it. On the flat sides of an angular body like a cube it ends at a straight border that far away instead: grooves and diamonds stop with a short wall, and only whole bumps stay. «Perfil» shapes the cross-section of a groove or joint: pointed and flat come out exactly, round in as many steps as «Detalhe» gives it.

Besides «Ranhuras», «Recartilhado», «Favo de mel» and «Saliências» there are more patterns. «Células» are irregular cells like paving stones or dried clay; their joints are cut cleanly as the honeycomb's are, and another «Disposição» lays them out anew. «Malha tricotada», «Corda» and «Entrelaçado de cestaria» copy knitted stitches, a wound rope and a basket of stakes and weavers; they start raised and round, at the size of their models. «Granulado» roughens the surface finely, as if blasted; the grain lies in space, without a seam or stretching. «Imagem» takes a grey picture as a height map: one of the ready ones such as wood, topography or terrazzo, or your own with «Carregar imagem personalizada…». Light becomes the full depth; «Largura do módulo» sets how wide a tile is, and under «Repetição» the tiles repeat, mirror or are staggered. A dark drawing on a transparent ground, such as black lines in an SVG, counts by its lines: they become the full depth. With «Uma vez» the image is pressed on a single time, like a label: «Posição angular (°)» and «Altura (%)» place its middle as for a text, «Largura da imagem» sets its width, and the surface beside it stays smooth. With faces picked, it always lands on them, even where «Posição angular (°)» and «Altura (%)» aim past them.

«Fibra de carbono (sarja)» lays carbon fibre woven in twill onto the body: upright bands and crossing bands, over and under each other, one band on from band to band, so the familiar diagonal shows. «Entrelaçamento» chooses «Sarja 2/2», the even weave of most carbon parts, or «Sarja 2/1» and «Sarja 3/1», where the upright bands show long and the crossing ones short. «Largura da faixa» sets how wide the upright bands are; «Largura das faixas transversais» makes the crossing ones wider or narrower for an uneven weave (0: as wide). Round a body the band width is rounded a little so the weave closes without a seam. The single fibres are far too fine for a print: the bands with their crossings are what shows.

«Tijolos» lay a brick wall onto the body, with joints sunk in like mortar. «Aparelho» chooses how the bricks are laid: «Aparelho a meia vez» as most walls are, «Aparelho alinhado», or with short bricks between the long ones («Aparelho inglês», «Aparelho inglês cruzado», «Aparelho flamengo»). «Comprimento dos tijolos» and «Altura da fiada» count from joint to joint and are rounded a little so that whole bricks fit: round a cup, from edge to edge of a box's side and from the bottom to the top; «Largura da junta» says how wide the joints are. Under «Mais», «Irregularidade dos tijolos (%)» lets every brick lie a little deeper, as in an old wall.

«Quadrados» and «Triângulos» lay tiles of one size in a grid onto the body, raised or pressed in, their walls cut steep and clean; the triangles stand in rows, pointing up and down in turn. «Tamanho dos quadrados» or «Tamanho dos triângulos» and «Folga» stay exactly as you set them – squares of 3.2 mm, 3.2 mm apart, are eight lines of a 0.4 mm nozzle each and print cleanly. The grid is centred on every face; round a round body the gap is rounded a little so that a whole number goes round. With «A partir da aresta inferior» the first row starts right at the bottom edge and reaches down into the first layer, where a brim holds it. For tiles on only the lower half of two sides, pick the two faces and put a helper body over the upper half with «Excluir textura» under «Máscara de textura» (see below). Under «Mais», the «Perfil» «Pontiagudo» makes pyramids of them, «Arredondado» and «Semicircular» cushions.

«Estrutura de madeira aparente» and «Parede de pedra» are made for model buildings, such as the houses of a model railway or a diorama. «Estrutura de madeira aparente» raises beams out of the wall, the plaster between them lying lower: posts «Largura dos painéis» apart, a sill and a plate to every storey of «Altura dos pisos», and «Travessas por piso» across it. «Contraventamento» chooses how much wood the panels hold: «Escoras diagonais» lean towards the middle from both ends, «Cruzes de Santo André» sit under the lowest rail, «Escoras nos cantos» in the top corners, and «Misto» puts braces at the ends with crosses and corner braces between, as on many old houses. «Largura das vigas» and «Altura do relevo das vigas» make the beams wide and deep, «Veios de madeira (%)» gives them a grain: 0 % none, below 50 % more and finer lines, above it two wide, deep grooves – from planed wood to rough planks. As with bricks, panels and storeys are rounded a little so that whole ones fit, from the bottom edge up. «Parede de pedra» lays an old wall of stones of different sizes in rough courses, the mortar joints lower and every stone bulging a little by its own amount. «Arredondamento (%)» goes from broken stone with sharp edges (0 %) to rounded field stones (100 %); «Variação do tamanho (%)», «Largura da junta» and «Disposição» say how different the stones are, how wide the joints and how they lie. Both are shape only, in one colour, so «Padrão como peça independente» can make the beams or the stones a part of their own in a second colour.

The pattern «Fissuras (kintsugi)» grows cracks across the surface as in kintsugi, with kinks, branches and a width that tapers towards the end. «Início» tells where they begin: at the top rim of a vase or a cup, at the bottom, from the rim to the middle of a plate, or anywhere; under «Tipo» they become lightning. With «Preenchimento dourado como peça independente» the notch is filled by a part of its own in gold, for a second filament; it goes along when you change or remove the texture. Under «Mais» you set branches, zigzag and chipped edges, and another «Semente» throws the cracks anew.

«Casca de árvore» lays a tree's bark round a log: «Carvalho», «Pinheiro», «Pícea», «Bétula» or «Faia», each at its own size and depth. «Veios de madeira» makes the body a piece of wood: under «Madeira» choose oak, ash, beech, pine or walnut, under «Corte» a log without its bark or a board, flat-sawn with its arches or quarter-sawn with straight lines. «Largura dos anéis» makes the grain fine or coarse. With «Anéis de crescimento nas extremidades» the ends of a log show the annual rings, and they match the grain on its sides: the rings run through the whole body as in a real piece of wood. Under «Mais» you add «Nós», and the rings bend round them.

With the pattern «Texto (aplicado)» you stick a text onto the body like a label pressed on: the surface is unrolled round the place, so the letters keep their size on a vase's belly, on a slanted wall or over the edge of a box. "Around" (0° is the front, 90° the right) and "Height" in % along the axis say where it goes; with the axis on X or Y, 0° is the top - that puts the text on a flat plate. «Direção» engraves it or raises it. Over a real corner it tears like a sticker; the status message says so then. «Letras de cima para baixo» stacks the letters top to bottom here too. With faces picked, the text always lands on them, even where «Posição angular (°)» and «Altura (%)» aim past them.

To keep part of the body smooth, or to texture only a part, use a helper body: put a box, a cylinder or a sphere where it should be, select it and choose under «Máscara de textura» either «Excluir textura» or «Textura apenas aqui». It turns transparent, and it counts when the other body gets its texture, also while it is hidden. Hide or delete it before printing.

The result is a mesh like an imported model, and it keeps the body it was made on. Select it later, also after saving, and the card shows the settings it was made with: change them and click «Alterar textura», and the texture is made again on that body, where and as large as the textured body stands now. «Remover textura» gives the plain body back. Mask bodies count again when the texture is changed: hide them rather than delete them if you may change it later. Undo takes back each of these steps as well.

For a print in two colours, switch on «Padrão como peça independente», with any pattern: the pattern becomes a part of its own, and «Cor do padrão» gives it its colour – to begin with one that stands out against the body, the next time the one you chose last. Out of the body, the part is what stands out, and the body stays as it was; into the body, the body gets the pattern cut in and the part fills the cut up to the surface, like the gold of the cracks. Both go together in a bundle: they move together, each keeps its colour, and a 3MF has them as two parts for the slicer. Change or remove the texture as before; the pattern part goes along. With several layers, all have to go the same way, out of the body or into it; a pattern going both ways stays one with the body.

Painting in several colours

For a print in several colours, «Pintar» colours parts of a body right in the design: a face, a round wall, the inside of a hole, a round patch or an area you draw round. It works like the paint tools of the slicers, but the paint is saved with the design. Select one body and click «Pintar» in the «Modificar» group, next to «Textura de superfície». The panel offers the colours of your design, and «Cor personalizada» mixes one of your own. Then paint in the view with one of three tools:

  • «Preenchimento»: a click fills the face up to its sharp edges, like the bucket of a paint program: the top of a box, the wall of a cylinder, the floor of a pocket or the inside of a hole, each in one click. «Parar em arestas com um ângulo superior a» says how sharp an edge has to be to stop the fill; at 90° it runs over the edges of a box.
  • «Círculo»: a click lays a round patch of the «Diâmetro» set onto the surface, centred where you click, on a curved surface too. It stops at the body's sharp edges and never comes through on the back of a wall.
  • «Laço»: hold the mouse button and draw round an area. What you see inside the shape is painted; the back of the body behind it is not.

«Borracha» takes the paint off again with the same tools, «Limpar tudo» takes all of it off at once. Every stroke is a step of its own, so Ctrl+Z takes the last one back. Between strokes the right mouse button turns the view as always; «Concluir» or Esc closes the panel.

The edges of a circle or a lasso are cut into the body's mesh, so a circle on the face of a box is round, not a few triangles, and the body stays closed. The paint belongs to the body: it moves and turns with it, stretches with it when you resize it, and a stroke that finds nothing any more after a change is left out. A 3MF export writes the paint as painted faces, which OrcaSlicer, Bambu Studio and PrusaSlicer print with their filaments (see Files and saving); an OBJ keeps the colours too, an STL stays one colour.

A group cut into one body, a box with its holes for instance, is painted as one body: paint it after cutting the holes, and its paint stays when you change the group in an open group. The parts of a bundle are painted one by one. A painted body that you group with others keeps its paint as a part and shows it again when you ungroup it. An imported mesh that is not closed is painted on its own triangles.

A vase

The «Vaso» is a body of its own for vases, pots and lampshades. Its measures are under «Propriedades», its form and pattern on the card «Forma e padrão»; all of it can be changed at any time, also after saving:

  • «Formato do sólido»: bottle, bellied, bowl with neck, barrel, cylinder or funnel. The height and the widest diameter are the shape's own measures: drag the handles, or type «Diâmetro» and «Altura».
  • «Secção transversal»: a circle, a polygon with rounded corners or a wave (soft, pointed, arches or fins). «Torção (°)» turns it up the height, «Oscilação (°)» lets it swing back and forth.
  • «Construção»: «Maciço (modo vaso)» is for the slicer's vase mode (also called spiralize): the slicer prints one wall in a spiral and leaves out the top and the infill, so the body is drawn solid. «Oco com parede» gives a real wall and bottom for a normal print. With «Fundo» at 0 mm the hollow vase has no bottom: a tube open at both ends, for bells, mouthpieces and pipes.
  • «Padrão»: a new vase is plain. To choose from are grooves, stripes, Voronoi cells or facets (low poly) on the outside, in a band of the height if you like; they belong to the vase and stay editable with it.

«Secção transversal no topo» blends the cross-section into a second one up the height, say from a circle at the bottom to a hexagon at the top.

«Desenhar o vaso», high up in the vase's settings, opens a large window of its own over the work area: in it you draw the vase yourself, in real millimetres. You move it by its title bar and make it larger from its corner; the vase in the view follows every change. «Formato do sólido» shows it from the side: drag the points, the top one sets the height, the widest one the diameter; «Controlo» gives a point an angle, «Canto» a kink. «Secção transversal» shows the cross-section from above, and the «Simetria» mirrors or repeats what you draw. «Torção» draws the twist as a curve up the height. An SVG file from a drawing program becomes the cross-section or the body form, the mesh of a model vase (STL, 3MF, OBJ) the body form. A photo of a vase can go behind the drawing to trace, or «Usar contorno» takes its outline. «Vetorizar» does the same with settings: «Limiar» for how clearly the object must stand out from the background, «Pontos» (3 to 40) and «Canto a partir de»; the new body form shows in red over the photo first and becomes the vase's with «Aplicar». Where the vase stands before a busy background (a shelf, a room), the search does not find it; then the «Laço magnético» catches it: click roughly round the vase, between two clicks the line follows the edge by itself, and a click on the first point, a double click or Enter closes it. The body form then comes from the lasso; «Descartar laço» lets the search look again. One drag of the mouse is one step of undo; while you drag, the view shows the vase roughly.

The card «Fundo e parede» holds what the body needs besides its form. On a hollow vase: drain holes with a slope towards them, a hollow foot, an open wall («Parede vazada»: Voronoi, honeycomb, diamonds or circles, for lanterns and baskets) and a «Abat-jour», hanging, standing on a socket or over an LED puck. On a solid vase, «Reforço do modo vaso» cuts fine slits through which the slicer prints ribs inside or a double wall in its vase mode, in one go. Recesses for rubber feet go with either. «Tem de reter água» raises the wall and bottom of a hollow vase to at least 1.6 mm.

On the card «Acessórios» the vase gets its accessories. «Pernas» can be moulded on, so they are part of the vase, or made to plug in, with sockets in the bottom; a stand holds the vase from below. A «Prato» catches the water, or hides in the foot. A hollow vase can take an «Peça interior»: a plant insert, one with a water store for a pot that waters itself, a holder for stems or water tubes. A «Tampa» slips over the rim, snaps into a groove or screws onto a thread in the wall. As a «Tampa de bule» the top of the vase itself becomes the lid, as on a teapot: «Altura da tampa» (or «Sólido até · tampa desde», from the bottom) sets how much, the pattern and the twist run on across the joint, a lip holds it in the opening, and «Pega (impressa separadamente)» adds a knob that is glued into a hole on top. «Dispor acessórios» lays the parts out beside the vase as objects of their own, ready to print, upside down where that prints better. The vase already has the sockets, groove or thread. After changing a setting, lay them out again: the parts from before are replaced. If a part does not fit this vase, the editor says so, for example when an insert would not get through a narrow neck.

The card «Impressão» tells what the vase takes to print: its weight in the chosen «Material» and the length of filament – for a solid vase worked out for the slicer's vase mode, one line along the wall. Below are notes on printing it: an overhang of more than 45° and where it is, a wall that is too thin, what a lid, a lamp or legs need, and the slicer settings for ribs and a double wall. A teapot lid is checked as it prints, upside down on its top: there a shoulder that narrows towards the rim overhangs.

«Detalhe» sets how finely the vase is divided into triangles: finer looks smoother, but makes the editor slower with large vases.
